title: Part IV: Melee dock, streets, church, grog machine fight, LeChuck, ending (DOS CD, SCUMM v5)

entry.notes: First frame of the 'Last Part' card: global/script-131.txt [0039] loadRoom(95), started by room-070-hellcliff/local-206.txt [046E] right after UserputOn [046C] (so no item slide survives into Part IV). Script 131 set Bit[453] (Part IV) and Var[277]=6 at global/script-131.txt [002F]/[0034]. THE CARD LASTS 129.8 s AND NO INPUT SHORTENS IT. 131 runs cutscene([]) with no beginOverride, so Esc does nothing (beginCutscene sets cutScenePtr to 0, engines/scumm/script.cpp:1631-1646; abortCutscene needs it, :1689-1709). The two prints are blanks, and the only exit is isSoundRunning(107) going false (global/script-131.txt [005B]-[0060]). Sound 107 is a CD-track resource: build/blocks-dos-cd/DISK_0001/LECF/LFLF_0095/SOUN_0107 has type byte 0x02 at +0x0F (engines/scumm/sound.cpp:315-324) and descriptor 06 01 00:00:00 00:00:00 at +0x18, i.e. track 6, one loop, from the start to the end of the track (engines/scumm/soundcd.cpp:226-251). The music driver plays no part. game/dos-cd/track6.flac is 5724180 samples at 44.1 kHz, 129.8 s, the same length as the redump's Track 06.bin. Measured: the unskipped Part One card, which waits on the same track (sound 104), lasted 7794 ticks (track 6 start at tick 7987, next track at tick 15781, out/runs/20261019T131143Z-run/trace.jsonl). Part One, Two and Three cards have overrides (room-096-part1/local-200.txt [0004], global/script-122.txt [0007], global/script-107.txt [00DD]); only this one does not. Save and load do not help: the CD track resumes at its saved position (engines/scumm/soundcd.cpp:345-397), and load time counts. Only a missing or short track 6 ends it early, and that is the No Music timing rules/anypercent.md bans (docs/anypercent/findings.md 'Music check'). Other levers checked and rejected: no item slide can be carried in (UserputOn above) or built (each dialogue choice runs UserputOff, then script 32 runs UserputOn: global/script-014.txt [00E2], global/script-032.txt [0011]). The dock ghost and the church are forced: 133 is started only by room-045-cu-church/local-200.txt [1594], and 733/734 become usable only inside it. Ctrl+W (global/script-004.txt [0257]-[02A6]) is banned. On the first room-83 frame the inventory is reduced to 823 (the 'magic seltzer bottle', renamed in global/script-106.txt [055B]); 488 and 733 would also be kept but are not owned (room-083-cu-dock/entry.txt [0020]-[0067]). Owning 823 is what starts the wedding scene (room-078-church/entry.txt [000E]-[0027]). Var[196]==3 (all trials, global/script-071.txt [0088]) keeps the street pirates off (global/script-047.txt [0000]). Bit[436]==0 (from S6) selects the Herman epilogue (global/script-146.txt [0170]); the crew variant (room 27) is about as long. Not expressible as a flag but required: 905 without class 6 (true unless the dock ghost was already met). Bit[51]==1 (ship bought; set only by global/script-056.txt [3F04] in S3, listed in S3's exit flags, and the only clear, global/script-056.txt [01A2], is on Stan's first-visit path) is required: when global 133 loads room 59, room-059-stans/entry.txt [0035]-[004C] starts local 201 if Stan (actor 3) is not in room 59, Bit[51] is 0 and Var[196] >= 3. Local 201 puts Stan in the room and starts global 56, his sales script (room-059-stans/local-201.txt [002F]-[003C]; global/script-056.txt [000D]-[002D]: VAR_VERB_SCRIPT=14, UserputOff, walks), which would collide with 133's fight. Stan is in room 0 since room-035-low-stree/entry.txt [007C] and Var[196]==3, so Bit[51] alone keeps it from starting. Church door 438: this file assumes it is CLOSED (state 0, entry flag). No Part I segment arranges the pirate-door window (see glitches), so closed is the default; the door-open variant is this file without the Open move and with {state 438 eq 1} at entry. The move format cannot skip a move, so that variant would be a separate file (open_questions).

moves.name: Dock: skip script 131's three ego text segments during the walk
moves.cite: global/script-131.txt [0077] breakHere, [0078] printEgo('Well, that was certainly easier than the trip TO Monkey Island.') + [00BB] WaitForMessage, [011C] (Bit[436]==0) printEgo('I wish those guys hadn't been so excited about getting sunscreen.' + wait() + 'Now I'll have to stop the wedding by myself!') with no wait, [018E] end; room-070-hellcliff/local-206.txt [046E] startScript(131,[]) (no F: not freeze-resistant); room-083-cu-dock/local-204.txt [0005] cutscene -> global/script-018.txt [0070] freezeScripts(127) (freezes 131), [00A3] endCutscene (unfreezes it); engines/scumm/actor.cpp:3530-3531 (actorTalk sets VAR_HAVE_MSG = 0xFF at once), engines/scumm/scumm.cpp:3382 (VAR_HAVE_MSG = _haveMsg each frame before the scripts run)
moves.note: Free: these presses fall inside the dock walk, which needs no other input. Why: left alone, 131 is still in WaitForMessage on its first line when local 204 starts (a 63-character line against a ~40-frame walk). 204's cutscene freezes it, [0083] print(255,' ') replaces its text, and after [00A3] it resumes as soon as the dialogue text clears, printing its two-segment second line in the middle of the dock dialogue. That line can satisfy the choose move's var-25 marker before the choice, and if 131 runs before script 14 in slot order its print re-arms VAR_HAVE_MSG and holds script 14's WaitForMessage ([00F7]) for two more segments, delaying the spray. With the three segments skipped here (about 6 frames), 131 has run [018E] long before the ghost appears. The until is the ghost's first frame (local-204 [0000] Var[277]=0, same frame as its beginOverride [0019]), as for the walk before this split: if only one '.' lands (an executor that sends one key per move), the move still ends on time for the ghost Esc, and only the interleave described in the next moves' notes remains. Local 204 prints nothing before its override ([0000]-[001B]), so no ghost text is caught here. Key-move convention (as in S3): press the key once on the first frame it can take effect (Esc only acts once the script has run beginOverride: abortCutscene does nothing while cutScenePtr is 0, engines/scumm/script.cpp:1689-1709), then press '.' on each new text segment (VAR_HAVE_MSG var 3 != 0; '.' sets _talkDelay = 0, engines/scumm/input.cpp:1418-1421; one press per wait() segment) until the until-conditions hold.

The way is up and left, so a walk restarted every frame gains ground (a fresh walk rounds each step away from zero: anypercent-engine-mechanics.md §2.5). reclick: true plays the executor's greedy re-clicks; reclick_sweep: true also tries a floor click every frame, alternating between two points ahead of ego (a new target each frame, so no restart is ignored), with the archway click on the frame that finishes first (executor._reclick_sweep), and keeps the faster. Measured from the S6#65 cut, first click to High Street: 67 frames with one click, 63 greedy, 60 sweep (points 16 and 40 px ahead won; six other pairs gave 63-67). 451's climb (local-205.txt) starts at ego's y, which is always the walk point's 88 (17 frames), then a scale-18 walk to (155,72) (8 frames); neither can be shortened.

Never right-click 438 after it is open (Var[182]=3 = Close); the next move enters with a left click (Walk to). 438 starts closed (out/objects.json state 0); only the player or Part I's wandering pirates change it (see glitches, rng_points). rng_points.what is random: Whether 438 is open (state 1) on entering Part IV. Wandering pirates (global/script-047.txt with Var[193]=200, only while Var[196]<3) run room-034-high-stre/local-200.txt: they enter through door index 4 (544,101) when Local[1]=getRandomNr(5)==4 or leave through it when Local[2]==4, opening 438 with global 25 and closing it with global 26 four frames later.
rng_points.how the seed/search should treat it: Part I segments decide it; S7 only reads state(438). If ego leaves room 34 inside a pirate's open-close window, startScene kills the local script (engines/scumm/room.cpp:80 killScriptsAndResources) and the door stays open for the rest of the game. Worth ~0.5 s in S7 (the Open sentence with its 20-jiffy reach); search Part I room-34 exits for it, never pay Part I time for it.

rng_points.what is random: Where a LeChuck punch sends Guybrush (rooms 43, 59, 32 or 83 via getRandomNr(2) and getRandomNr(1), VAR_FIXEDDISK being 1). The first punch from the church is scripted to Stan's (global/script-133.txt [00CD]).
rng_points.how the seed/search should treat it: Failure path only: the route never moves ego after script 129, so no punch and no draw matters. A branch that triggers a punch should be discarded, not reseeded.

record_comparison: Record (saruya, 21:52, DOS CD): Part IV = 2:07.0, 19:45.5 ('Last Part' card) to 21:52.4 (fade). Frames: dock reply 'I LOVE root beer!' 19:53, church 20:12, grog machine fight 20:18-20:51, ending 20:51-21:52 (61 s) (docs/research/anypercent-runner-sources.md §2.1, §2.6). THE CARD DOMINATES: with the CD audio our rules require (rules/anypercent.md 'Music check'; the user confirms the audio tracks are on the disc), the card waits for all of CD track 6, 129.8 s: the official disc's Track 06.bin (redump zip in ~/Downloads/torrents/TheSecretOfMonkeyIslandUSAEnFrDeEsIt) is 22896720 bytes = 129.80 s at 176400 B/s, with no pregap in the cue, the same length as game/dos-cd/track6.flac. The record cannot have waited for it, and its own numbers bound its card: the dock reply came 7.5 s after the card's first frame, and the dock part alone needs about 3.5-4 s (ego's 265-px walk from (80,121) to (345,121) at WalkSpeed(8,2), the last WalkSpeed write on S6's path being room-012-monkey-he/entry.txt [0049], ~6.5 px/frame as measured on the Part I dock = ~41 frames = ~3.4 s; then the Esc, the menu, the choice, ego's line; and 'I LOVE root beer!' is the third segment of the ghost's reply, room-083-cu-dock/local-204.txt [020F]). So the record's card lasted about 4 s at most. That contradicts runner-sources §2.1 ('at least 6 s'), so one of the two readings is wrong; either way the record's setup had no track 6 or a much shorter one. With the rules as they stand, S7 is about 124-126 s slower than the record's split on the card alone. The rest is a script model of this route (12 frames/s at VAR_TIMER_NEXT 5, delays in 1/60 s; estimates, not measured). The ending is ~58-60 s of fixed time (script 132 with the forced instant replay ~20.5 s, 137 ~13.5 s, 151 ~3.5 s, 138 with the Stan and Herman cutaways ~21 s: five waited lines before menu 1, seven epilogue segments, one line after each menu), so the record's 61 s leaves only text-skip latency. Dock to church (19 s in the record) holds the ~6 s unskippable spray animation and three walks, where only input latency, shmoovement and the 1-frame right-click Open gain. The church entry to the start of script 132 is ~23 s in the model (walk-ins ~3 s, ~25 input/text frames, 133's unskippable ~15 s including Guybrush's 55-frame + 240-jiffy daze, wake-up 1 s, Use with the 20-jiffy reach) against ~39 s in the record (20:12-20:51). The menu-3 choice explains part of that gap only if the runner gave a single Esc after '4' and let [1490]'s punch (~7.3 s) play; with two Escs '4' costs one frame more than the dentist line, which is all this route gains there. The other candidates are unskipped overrides (map, Stan's two) and input latency. Excluding the card: expect a few seconds of gain outside the church and fight, and up to ~10-15 s inside it, depending on what the video shows. Re-measure the card and the 20:12-20:51 stretch from the video.
open_questions: RULES DECISION, affects the whole run: the 'Last Part' card waits for all of CD track 6. The official disc's track 6 is 129.8 s (redump Track 06.bin, 22896720 bytes, no pregap; equal to game/dos-cd/track6.flac), and the user confirms the audio is on the disc, so under rules/anypercent.md ('playing': false is invalid) the CD-audio requirement alone costs ~124 s here against the record.
